source_refs.note: Exercise 1.5, Question 7 (book page 33); answers PDF 301 (book page 299)

blocks.prompt: 7 (i) A quantity changes according to \(N = 500e^{kt}\). If \(N = 250\) when \(t = 5\), find: the value of constant \(k\).
blocks.explanation:
The quantity falls from 500 to 250 in 5 units of time, so this is decay and \(k\) will be negative.
We must find \(k\) from the pair \(t = 5\), \(N = 250\).
Plan: substitute, divide by 500, take \(\ln\), divide by 5.
steps:
Given: \(N = 500e^{kt}\); \(N = 250\) when \(t = 5\).
To find: the constant \(k\).
Method: isolate \(e^{5k}\) and take \(\ln\).

Substitute \(t = 5\) and \(N = 250\)
\[250 = 500e^{5k}\]
Why: the known pair satisfies the model.

Make the exponential stand alone
\[\dfrac{1}{2} = e^{5k}\]
Why: divide by 500: \(\frac{250}{500} = \frac{1}{2}\).

Take \(\ln\) of both sides
\[\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 5k\]
\[-\ln 2 = 5k\]
Why: \(\ln(e^{5k}) = 5k\), and \(\ln\frac{1}{2} = -\ln 2\).

Solve for \(k\)
\[k = -\dfrac{\ln 2}{5}\]
\[= -\dfrac{0.693147}{5}\]
\[\approx -0.13863\]
Why: divide by 5. \(k < 0\): the quantity is decaying.

blocks.prompt: 7 (ii) A quantity changes according to \(N = 500e^{kt}\). If \(N = 250\) when \(t = 5\), find: the quantity \(N\) when \(t = 10\).
blocks.explanation:
Now \(k\) is known from part (i); the unknown \(N\) is not in the exponent.
We substitute \(t = 10\) and calculate.
Plan: use the exact \(k = -\frac{\ln 2}{5}\) so that \(10k = -2\ln 2\), and simplify exactly.
steps:
Given: \(N = 500e^{kt}\) with \(k = -\frac{\ln 2}{5}\) (from part (i)), and \(t = 10\).
To find: \(N\) at \(t = 10\).
Method: direct substitution; the exact value of \(k\) avoids rounding error.

Find \(10k\)
\[10k = 10 \times \left(-\dfrac{\ln 2}{5}\right)\]
\[= -2\ln 2\]
Why: this is the exponent we need.

Substitute
\[N = 500e^{-2\ln 2}\]
\[= 500e^{\ln(2^{-2})}\]
Why: \(-2\ln 2 = \ln(2^{-2})\) by the power law of logarithms.

Check
With the rounded value: \(500e^{-1.3863} \approx 500 \times 0.25 = 125\).
Also: the quantity halves every 5 units, so in 10 units it halves twice: \(500 \to 250 \to 125\) \(\checkmark\)
